3. The High Court Division by the impugned Judgment made the Rule absolute directing the petitioners to "mutate the names of the petitioners (writ-petitioners) in respect of the land in record-of-right upon changing ownership/possession of the land" within three months observing that in view of the judgments of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 5380 of 1991 and writ petition No.4997 of 2008, the petitioners are under obligation to mutate the disputed property in favour of the writ-petitioners under sections 143 and 143(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Against the said judgment and order, the writ-respondent Nos. 1-4 preferred Civil Petition No. 1718 of 2010. One Samar Chakrabartee and 4 others who are not parties in the writ petition preferred Civil Petition No. 869 of 2011 against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division stating, inter alia, that they instituted Other Class Suit No. 197 of 2011 in the 3rd Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong seeking declaration that the deed dated 11th February, 2009 is forged, collusive and not binding upon them, that the writ-petitioners' predecessors AKM Bashir Ahmed and others executed a collusive agreement with the writ-petitioners and that the writ-respondents obtained a collusive decree. They claimed title and ownership of the disputed property by way of amicable partition; the BS Khatian was prepared behind their back, and the High Court Division without affording them any opportunity passed the impugned judgment which is not binding upon them. 

 4. Lieutenant Colonel (Retd) Zillur Rahman and 19 others preferred Civil Petition No. 2686 of 2010 challenging the same judgment of the High Court Division stating that the owner Saifuddin Ahmed Siddiqui sold the disputed property in favour of AKM Bashir Ahmed and 3 others by registered deed dated 19th December, 1962. The said purchasers sold the same lands to Lieutenant Colonel (Retd) Zillur Rahman and after the death of AKM Bashir Ahmed, the petitioner Nos. 3-8 and 17 inherited the remaining land. During the last survey operation the disputed property was recorded in the name of the Government but on appeal by AKM Bashir Ahmed and others, the settlement officers directed for correction of the record-of-rights and a separate Khatian was prepared in their names. The writ petitioners in collusion with Saifuddin Ahmed Siddiqui instituted the suit for Specific Performance of Contract. The decree passed in the suit is not binding upon them as they were not made parties. They had no knowledge about the decree passed in the civil suit and the Judgment in Writ Petition No. 4997 of 2008. Those suit and writ petition were instituted upon untrue allegations of fact. 5. Mr. Rajik-al-Jalil, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the petitioners in Civil Petition No. 1718 of 2010 argued that the disputed property is the khas land of the Government as the vendor of the writ-petitioners surrendered the same as excess land under PO 98 of 1972 and in that view of the matter, the High Court Division erred in law in directing for correcting the record-of-right in favour of the writ-petitioners. It is further contended that the High Court Division acted in excess of power in directing the petitioners to mutate the names of the writ-petitioners in the record-of-rights in failing to consider that their .application for mutation has not been disposed of in accordance with law and pending determination of the matter, the High Court Division cannot give such direction. 

 13. Rule 24(4) provides that when the land vests in or comes to the possession of the Government, it shall be recorded in the khas khatian. Thus, there is no gainsaying fact that the mutation of record-of-rights requires enquiry, perusal of previous settlement records, collector's record and the annexed Register. These Rules show that the mutation of the record-of-rights is not mere routine work rather such mutation requires examination of the records which may take time. The writ-petitioners without awaiting the decision of the Revenue Officer moved the High Court Division by making a mere statement that the Revenue Officer refused their prayer.
